requirements.applies_when: You operate in the construction industry and have one or more employees. Unlike the general rule (non-construction employers need 4+ employees, covered in round 1), ANY construction employer with 1+ employees must carry workers' compensation coverage — and owners count: corporate officers and LLC members are considered employees for this purpose unless they hold a valid Certificate of Election to be Exempt.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. ch. 440; Division of Workers' Compensation, Coverage Requirements page
requirements.fees: unverified (premiums set by licensed carriers; not published as a fixed schedule)
requirements.notes: Construction-only rule; builds on round 1 general findings. The Division lists which trades are 'construction industry' at Fla. Admin. Code 69L-6.021 (linked from the coverage page).
requirements.timeline: unverified (coverage must be in place once the employer meets the threshold; no statutory deadline published on the coverage page)
requirements.title: Workers' compensation — construction industry mandatory coverage (1+ employees)

requirements.applies_when: A construction contractor subcontracts any part of its work. Before the subcontractor begins work, the contractor must verify the subcontractor has workers' compensation coverage (documentation requirements at Fla. Admin. Code 69L-6.032) — if not, the subcontractor's employees become the statutory employees of the contractor, and the contractor pays benefits for any work-related injury, illness, or fatality.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. ch. 440; Division of Workers' Compensation, Coverage Requirements page ('Contractors' section)
requirements.notes: This is the construction-specific operational duty — a general contractor cannot rely on a sub's promise of coverage; uninsured subs' workers legally become the contractor's employees.
requirements.timeline: Verification must occur BEFORE the subcontractor begins work on the project
requirements.title: Workers' compensation — construction contractor subcontractor-verification duty

requirements.applies_when: A corporate officer of a construction business wants to be exempt from workers' comp coverage for themselves. Corporation must be registered and active with the Florida Division of Corporations; applicant must be listed as an officer in those records AND attest to minimum 10% ownership. Strictly limited: no more than three officers of a corporation or any group of affiliated corporations (including LLCs) may elect to be exempt.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 440.05; Division of Workers' Compensation, Construction Industry exemption page
requirements.fees: $50.00 application fee (non-construction exemptions are free). The Division warns service fees may also apply.

forms.name: Certificate of Election to be Exempt — online application (Division of Workers' Compensation)

requirements.notes: Compare round 1 non-construction rules: no fee and no limit on number of exempt corporate officers. Construction is far stricter (3-officer cap, $50 fee). Applicant cannot be affiliated with an ACTIVE Stop Work Order or Working in Violation, and cannot have an associated insufficient payment.
requirements.timeline: Exemptions valid for 2 years; effective/expiration dates listed on the Certificate. Renewal requires a valid state driver's license not expired more than 30 days at submission.
requirements.title: Workers' compensation construction exemption — corporate officers (max 3, $50 fee)

requirements.applies_when: An LLC member of a construction business wants to be exempt from workers' comp coverage for themselves. LLC must be registered and active with the Florida Division of Corporations; applicant must attest to minimum 10% ownership. Limit: no more than three members of an LLC or any group of affiliated LLCs (including corporations) may elect to be exempt.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 440.05; Division of Workers' Compensation, Construction Industry exemption page
requirements.fees: $50.00 application fee per applicant; service fees may also apply

forms.name: Certificate of Election to be Exempt — online application (Division of Workers' Compensation)

requirements.notes: Compare non-construction LLC rule: up to 10 members exempt, no fee. Exemption is issued to the individual, not the business — a separate application per person per entity. A valid state driver's license is required to obtain or renew.
requirements.timeline: Valid for 2 years; renew before expiration. Customer service: (850) 413-1609, wc_exemption@myfloridacfo.com
requirements.title: Workers' compensation construction exemption — LLC members (max 3, $50 fee)

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources (RER), Construction Trades Qualifying Board
requirements.applies_when: You do contracting work in Miami-Dade County in a trade category that is NOT covered by a State of Florida certified contractor license. State-certified contractors need NO further county license (state preempts local licensing; they only register with the County Building Department). County Certificates of Competency cover local-only categories issued under Chapter 10 of the Miami-Dade County Code — general/building/residential contractors and specialty trades (electrical, plumbing, mechanical, roofing, swimming pool, maintenance, and building specialties).
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Code ch. 10; s. 163.211, F.S. (HB 735 preemption, effective July 1, 2021)
requirements.fees: $315 application fee for the personal certificate, plus an additional $315 for the business portion of the license

forms.name: Contractor application (personal certificate, then separate business application)

requirements.notes: Key overlay rule from county-sourced FAQ: 'License by the state means the state approved and issued a license and no further licensing is required by the county.' Since July 1, 2023, HB 735 eliminated many local-only specialty categories (e.g., caulking, flooring, painting, ornamental iron); work in eliminated categories now needs a state or county license only if the scope requires a building permit. RER offers a registration program for state-licensed contractors.
requirements.timeline: unverified for initial issuance; renewals every two years with continuing education credits required
requirements.title: Miami-Dade County Certificate of Competency — when required on top of a state license

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources (RER), Contractor Licensing Section
requirements.applies_when: You apply for a Miami-Dade County Certificate of Competency (general, building, or residential contractor, or a specialty trade) to do permitted work in the county.
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Code ch. 10; Miami-Dade County Building Contractor Licenses / Building Specialty Licenses pages
requirements.fees: $315 personal certificate application fee; additional $315 for the business portion

forms.name: Business Application (post-exam) — filed after personal certificate approved

requirements.notes: Requirements: 1-4 years proven field experience (trade-dependent), application with employer letters stating dates of employment and description of work plus W-2s covering the employment period, passing exam (70%+). Non-exam specialty categories require 16 hours of classroom training before issuance (incl. 1 hour each: workplace safety/OSHA, business practices, workers' comp, laws and rules). Licensed contractors must maintain general liability and workers' comp insurance in effect at all times; doing business without meeting requirements draws citations under Chapter 10.
requirements.timeline: Exam: open-book, 70% or above to pass; book list provided at application. Proof of liability and workers' compensation insurance required after Board approval. Apply/inquire: Contractor Licensing Section, 786-315-2880, ContractorLicensing@miamidade.gov, Herbert S. Saffir Permitting and Inspection Center, 11805 SW 26 Street, Miami, FL 33175
requirements.title: Miami-Dade County contractor certificate — application requirements

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources (RER), Construction Trades Qualifying Board
requirements.applies_when: You need to know which local license category matches your trade before applying (county categories are distinct from state CILB categories).
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Code ch. 10; Construction Trades Qualifying Board rules and procedures
requirements.fees: unverified (application fee per category; see FL_DRAFT_COPS_0006)
requirements.notes: CTQB lists Building categories (General Contractor, Building Contractor, Residential Contractor — none include roofing or swimming pool), Building Specialties (concrete forming/placing, demolition, drywall, fence, glass & glazing, lathing & plastering, metal awning & storm shutter, misc. metals, pneumatic concreting, prestressed precast, reinforcing steel, roof, rook deck, screen enclosure, sign non-electric, structural steel, swimming pool, unit masonry and others), and Maintenance categories (Building Maintenance, Maintenance Electrician, Mechanical Maintenance, Plumbing Maintenance). Note: HB 735 eliminated some of these categories after 2023-07-01; the current live list on the CTQB page should be checked before relying on it.

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources (RER), Building Department
requirements.applies_when: Anyone who wants to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish, or change the occupancy of a building or structure, or erect/install/alter/repair/remove/convert/replace electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing systems regulated by the technical codes in Miami-Dade County.
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Code; Florida Building Code; 'How to Apply for Permits' page
requirements.fees: unverified (see Building Fee Schedule; some permits e.g. defective Chinese drywall expedite program waive fees)

forms.name: Building permit application (via the County Portal / E-permitting system)

requirements.notes: Application may be filed by an owner, authorized agent, or contractor. The County process covers properties with folios starting with '30' (unincorporated Miami-Dade); each municipality has its own Building Official issuing permits within city limits. Plans must remain at the construction site with the address posted and visible from the street; inspection is required before covering any part of the construction. Special (threshold) inspectors' work is in addition to mandatory Department inspections.
requirements.timeline: unverified (updated Construction and Permitting Procedures apply; inspections performed Mon-Fri 8:00 a.m.-3:30 p.m.)
requirements.title: Who may obtain a Miami-Dade building permit — licensed contractor vs owner

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County RER (Contractor Licensing / Building); Fla. Stat. ch. 489
requirements.applies_when: A construction business wants to pull permits for work in Miami-Dade County. A licensed contractor is required unless the property owner qualifies for and completes the owner-builder process.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. ch. 489 (ss. 489.103(7) owner-builder exemption, 489.126, 489.127); Miami-Dade County Code ch. 10
requirements.fees: Owner-builders may request a fee reduction via the Reduced Fee Owner Builder Permit Process Disclosure Statement; commercial owner-builder work capped at $75,000 cost

forms.name: Owner-Builder Disclosure Statement (must be reviewed before applying)

requirements.notes: Operational guardrails from the county's Contractor & Owner/Builder Responsibilities page: s. 489.127 prohibits a contractor from letting an uncertified person use his certification and from obtaining permits without first having a contract (first-degree misdemeanor; felony on subsequent violation); s. 489.126 requires permits applied for within 30 days of receiving >10% of the residential contract price, and work started within 90 days of permit issuance; s. 489.1425 requires written notice of the Construction Industry Recovery Fund in residential contracts over $2,500. Owner-builder is limited to the owner's own use/occupancy (not for sale/lease); commercial building at a cost of $75,000 or less in any 12-month period; the owner must provide direct onsite supervision and ensure all hired persons hold required licenses and insurance. For a construction business, the practical rule: commercial work above $75,000 must be done by a licensed contractor.
requirements.timeline: Owner-builder permit issued only upon passing an owner-builder validation appointment (Small Business and Homeowner Permitting Assistance Team); if validation is failed, a licensed contractor must apply for the permit and complete the work
requirements.title: Licensed contractor requirement and owner-builder alternative for permits

requirements.applies_when: A construction business scopes permitting for a commercial project in unincorporated Miami-Dade County.
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Building Department — Common Permits & Certificates
requirements.fees: unverified (fee sheets break down cost by permit category; e.g., electrical '01' category covers commercial work)
requirements.notes: Permit types published by the County: Master, Shop Drawings, Revision, Extension, Reissue, Supplemental, Demolition, Change of Contractor, Signs, and Environmental permits; trade categories (electrical categories include temp power for construction — Cat 14, temp for test — Cat 15 elevators/26 commercial-residential); Certificate of Occupancy/Completion required after final inspection and satisfaction of completion holds (temporary CO/TCC valid 90 days, extensions possible with trade and Fire approvals). County Building Fee Schedule governs permit fees; electrical permit page: http://www.miamidade.gov/global/economy/building/permits/electrical.page.
requirements.title: Miami-Dade permit types relevant to commercial construction work

requirements.agency: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (federal)
requirements.applies_when: A construction business operates in Florida and needs to know which agency's safety standards apply to its jobsites.
requirements.citation: OSH Act s. 18; OSHA State Plans FAQ; OSHA standard interpretation (2010-10-28)
requirements.notes: Verified negative finding: Florida does NOT have an OSHA-approved state plan — OSHA states expressly that 'Florida does not have an OSHA-approved state plan,' and OSHA's state-plan FAQ lists the 22 approved state-plan states/territories without Florida. Consequence: private-sector construction workers in Florida are covered DIRECTLY by federal OSHA (no Florida-specific construction safety standards overlay). Federal OSHA standards (e.g., 29 CFR 1926 construction standards) apply as written; there is no state construction safety program to register with or state-specific safety permit to obtain. State and local government workers are generally not covered by federal OSHA in non-state-plan states.
requirements.title: Workplace safety jurisdiction — Florida has no OSHA-approved state plan
